value.statement: For every Borel extended metric space X, set A⊆X and d:NNReal, if Measure.hausdorffMeasure (↑d) A=⊤, then ↑d≤dimH(A).

source.statement: For every Borel extended metric space X, set A⊆X and d:NNReal, if Measure.hausdorffMeasure (↑d) A=⊤, then ↑d≤dimH(A).
hypotheses: The Hausdorff measure at NNReal exponent d equals top.

patches.value: For D>0 fix 0<s<D. For a>0 define C_a(A,δ)=inf{∑'ᵢ ediam(Uᵢ)^a : U:ℕ→Set(X), A⊆⋃ᵢUᵢ and ∀i ediam(Uᵢ)≤δ}. Empty members have diameter zero and hence zero cost for a>0. In M008, the supremum over nonempty witnesses is the ordinary power for a nonempty member and zero for the empty member; thus its inner infimum is exactly this content and H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0}C_a(A,δ), with no normalization factor. If δ₁≤δ₂, every δ₁-admissible cover is δ₂-admissible, so C_a(A,δ₁)≥C_a(A,δ₂). The one-sided limit as scale decreases to zero therefore equals this supremum: positive scales are cofinal at zero and contents are monotone in this direction. M001 gives H^s(E)=∞; hence for every finite K all sufficiently small positive δ have C_s(E,δ)>K. Fix δ>0 and any countable δ-cover (Vᵢ) of F. Set ρᵢ=ediam(Vᵢ), Aᵢ=π₁(Vᵢ), Bᵢ=π₂(Vᵢ). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz in the concatenated Euclidean metric, so diam(Aᵢ),diam(Bᵢ)≤ρᵢ≤δ. In interval-length formulas use the underlying real diameter ρᵢ; in ENNReal content sums use its canonical ENNReal coercion. Given ε>0 set ηᵢ=ε2^(−i−1)/(1+ρᵢ^s)>0, with ε,ρᵢ interpreted as real numbers. If Bᵢ is nonempty it is bounded; extend its infimum/supremum enclosure by total width ηᵢ to obtain open Jᵢ⊇Bᵢ of length ≤ρᵢ+ηᵢ. If Bᵢ is empty choose any open interval of length ηᵢ. For every t∈[0,1] and x∈E, (x,t) lies in some Vᵢ, so x∈Aᵢ and t∈Bᵢ⊆Jᵢ. Thus the Aᵢ with t∈Jᵢ cover E at scale δ. From the infimum definition C_s(E,δ)≤∑'ᵢ1_{Jᵢ∩[0,1]}(t)ρᵢ^s pointwise on [0,1]. Put ν=volume.restrict([0,1]) on ambient Borel ℝ. For integration on all ℝ multiply the left side by 1_[0,1]; outside [0,1] both sides vanish, so the inequality holds everywhere. Every Jᵢ∩[0,1] is Borel; its indicator multiplied by ρᵢ^s is measurable and AEMeasurable for ν. The ambient mass is ν(ℝ)=volume([0,1])=ofReal(1−0)=1 by restriction and M011; hence ν is finite and ν([0,1])=1. Integrating the left side gives C_s(E,δ)ν([0,1])=C_s(E,δ), by M010 on [0,1] with constant C_s(E,δ). M009 monotonicity bounds this by the integral of the series. Apply M002 to interchange the ℕ-indexed sum and lintegral; countability and AEMeasurability were checked. M010 gives each summand integral as ρᵢ^sν(Jᵢ∩[0,1]). For S=Jᵢ∩[0,1], restriction gives ν(S)=volume(S∩[0,1])=volume(S). Enclose S in a closed interval of length at most ρᵢ+ηᵢ (if S is empty any singleton interval suffices). M013 gives volume(S)≤volume of the enclosure, and M011 evaluates that as ofReal(length)≤ofReal(ρᵢ+ηᵢ). Therefore C_s(E,δ)≤∑'ᵢρᵢ^(s+1)+∑'ᵢηᵢρᵢ^s≤∑'ᵢρᵢ^(s+1)+ε, using ρᵢ^s(ρᵢ+ηᵢ)=ρᵢ^(s+1)+ηᵢρᵢ^s and ∑ᵢ2^(−i−1)=1. For this fixed cover ε is arbitrary: if its (s+1)-cost is finite, ε↓0 gives C_s(E,δ)≤that cost; if infinite the inequality is immediate. Taking the infimum over all Nat-indexed δ-covers yields C_s(E,δ)≤C_(s+1)(F,δ). As δ decreases to zero the left side diverges, so the right side diverges; by M008 H^(s+1)(F)=⊤. Apply M014, the theorem that top Hausdorff measure at NNReal exponent s+1 implies that exponent is at most dim_H(F), to obtain s+1≤dim_H(F). This holds for every 0<s<D, so taking the supremum over s gives D+1≤dim_H(F). Use NNReal coercions in dimension theorems and corresponding real exponents in M008.
Instantiate le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_eq_top with product ambient space, set F, and NNReal exponent coercion of s+1.
The preceding argument established Hausdorff measure of F at the coercion of s+1 equals top; the ambient space is extended metric, Borel and measurable.
